The same above.
Is this still required?  What is the error if you just take the defaults and avoid setting CRYPTOGRAPHY_OPENSSL_NO_LEGACY?

Yes, it’s still required. Without CRYPTOGRAPHY_OPENSSL_NO_LEGACY=1, you will hit the following error:

```
|     from cryptography.hazmat.bindings._rust import openssl as rust_openssl
| RuntimeError: OpenSSL 3.0's legacy provider failed to load. This is a fatal error by default, but cryptography supports running without legacy algorithms by setting the environment variable CRYPTOGRAPHY_OPENSSL_NO_LEGACY. If you did not expect this error, you have likely made a mistake with your OpenSSL configuration.
| WARNING: exit code 1 from a shell command.
```
The mentioned bug has been closed for over a year.  Do we understand why the no-engines workaround mentioned in the bug doesn't work here?

It seems we can use OPENSSL_MODULES to point to the correct provider modules, rather than relying on CRYPTOGRAPHY_OPENSSL_NO_LEGACY. I will update in the next commit.
```
export OPENSSL_MODULES="${STAGING_LIBDIR_NATIVE}/ossl-modules"
```
This should always produce the image, right?  Why is this needed?  Maybe add a comment why it's needed?

It fix "devtool build-image obmc-phosphor-image" failed. Refer to
https://github.com/AspeedTech-BMC/openbmc/commit/5b2845132ba4f32f9b0d19e028ed3a067e6ecdbf

from that "because this recipes is used for building SPL and SPL should not be installed into rootfs."  This option doesn't control install, it controls whether a recipe is allowed to be empty.  I suspect in these cases, you need to optionally include the package, rather than just blanket allowing empty here.
I will remove in the next commit.
